title: Add Up the Valid Numbers
oneLiner: Parse a list of text values, skip the ones that aren't whole numbers, and total the rest: try/catch versus TryParse.
keyTakeaway: Bad input is expected, so handle it per item and keep going. In C#, int.TryParse returns false instead of throwing; in Python, wrap int(...) in try/except ValueError. Keep the try block around just the risky call.
explanation:
You get a list of strings, as you might read from a CSV file or a form. Return the sum of the ones that are valid whole numbers, ignoring the rest. Surrounding spaces and a leading + or - are fine (" 7 ", "+5", "-3"); decimals such as "3.5", empty strings and words are not.

In Python, int(text) handles all the valid forms and raises ValueError for everything else, so: loop, and inside the loop try: total += int(text) with except ValueError: pass (skipping is the whole point here, so an empty except body is right for once; it catches only ValueError).

In C#, int.Parse behaves the same way, throwing FormatException, and a try/catch works. The more idiomatic C# is if (int.TryParse(text, out int n)) total += n;: no exception, just a bool saying whether it worked. Exceptions in .NET are relatively slow, which matters when lots of the input is bad.
